samples.summary: Preserving `spillAnchor` through `compactCell` makes cell styles on spill ghosts non-durable: the calculator rewrites every ghost with `setCell(ghostRef, { v, spillAnchor })` and no `s`, so any style a user applies to a spilled cell is silently discarded on the next recalculation of the anchor. Before this change a style write stripped `spillAnchor`, so the cell stopped being a ghost and kept its style (at the cost of blocking the spill). The diff's own test only asserts the displayed value, not that the style survives a recalc. The fix belongs in calculator.ts (carry the existing ghost's `s` into the rewrite).
samples.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/calculator.ts:141 — `await sheet.setCell(ghostRef, { v: values[dr]?.[dc] ?? '', spillAnchor: sref });` writes the ghost with no style field, overwriting whatever `compactCell` (style-mutation.ts:61-85) now preserves on the ghost.

samples.summary: `omitStyleKeys` can return an empty `{}` style, and `unsetRangeStyleValues` writes that empty object straight to the sheet/column/row layers (sheet.ts:4436-4467) — unlike the range-patch branch, which drops empties. Downstream style resolution treats a present-but-empty layer as 'styled': `Sheet.resolveEffectiveStyle` and `resolveWorksheetCellStyle` both return `{}` instead of `undefined` for an otherwise unstyled cell, and the Yorkie document keeps a permanent empty `colStyles['1'] = {}` / `sheetStyle = {}` entry that never gets cleaned up. The diff's own row/column/sheet round-trip tests avoid `toBeUndefined()` and only check `style?.dp`, which hides this.
samples.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-grid.ts:117 `if (!sheetStyle && !colStyle && !rowStyle && !rangeStyle && !cell) return undefined;` — an empty `{}` colStyle is truthy, so the function now returns `{}`; same shape at packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:883. Written by packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store.ts:719 / :780 with the empty object.

samples.summary: `isDefaultLikeStyle` in the frontend still encodes the pruning rule this diff removes: it treats `dp === 2` as a default. Now that `dp` is never pruned from stored styles, an explicitly stored `dp: 2` (e.g. two Increase clicks on a plain cell, or an xlsx import at packages/sheets/src/import/xlsx-styles.ts:229) is a deliberate user choice, yet paint-format treats such a source cell as 'default-like' and copies a default style instead of the real one. Frontend has no `tsc`/lint lane over this, so nothing else will flag the stale assumption.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/sheet-view.tsx:62 `const isDefaultDecimalPlaces = style.dp === undefined || style.dp === 2;` feeding `isDefaultLikeStyle` at :341 (`const useDefaultStyle = isDefaultLikeStyle(sourceStyle);`), mirroring the `dp: 2` entry the diff deleted from `DefaultStyleValues`.

samples.summary: `resetRangeStyleToDefault` ('clear formatting') appends `DefaultResetStylePatch`, which contains no `dp` key. With `dp` now never pruned and written on every Increase/Decrease as a range patch, a cleared range keeps its stored `dp` in a lower patch; it is inert while `nf` is reset to `'plain'`, but the residue survives the clear and reappears the moment any later layer sets a numeric `nf`. Worth confirming that clear-formatting is expected to leave `dp` behind.
samples.evidence: packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:144-157 `DefaultResetStylePatch` lists b/i/u/st/borders/tc/bg/al/va/nf but no `dp`; used at sheet.ts:3763 `await this.addRangeStylePatch(range, DefaultResetStylePatch);`
